senses.definition: To leave something or someone completely and without intending to return; to give up completely.

examples.sentence: He was so upset that he decided to abandon his plans for the vacation.
examples.definition: He gave up his plans for the vacation because he was too upset.

examples.sentence: The crew had no choice but to abandon ship when the storm hit.
examples.definition: The crew had to leave the ship when the storm arrived.

idioms.definition: To leave a sinking ship, especially in a panic or without concern for others.
To give up all hope or expectation of success; to despair.

phrases.definition: to let oneself be carried away by something, especially a strong feeling such as pleasure or passion
to leave a child without parental care or protection

senses.definition: The power or capacity to do something or act in a certain way

examples.sentence: His ability to solve complex math problems impresses everyone.
examples.definition: His capacity or skill in solving difficult mathematical equations leaves others amazed.

examples.sentence: She lacks the ability to learn foreign languages quickly.
examples.definition: She struggles to acquire fluency in new languages as fast as others do.

idioms.idiom: an ability to turn the tables
idioms.definition: The power or skill to make a sudden change in a situation so that one gains advantage over others.
To be too difficult or complicated for someone to understand, beyond their ability level.

phrases.phrase: She has the ability to persuade anyone.
phrases.definition: She possesses the power to convince anyone with her arguments and charisma.

phrases.phrase: His abilities have greatly improved over time.
phrases.definition: There has been a significant increase in his skills and competencies throughout his development.
